:::{#exr-main-diagonal-practice}
#### The main diagonal of a tall matrix

The [main diagonal](#def-main-diagonal) of a [matrix](#def-matrix) that is not [square](#def-square-matrix)
stops when it runs out of [row](#def-matrix-row)s or [column](#def-matrix-column)s,
whichever comes first.
A tall matrix, with more rows than columns, runs out of columns first.
Let

$$
\matr{E} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & -2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 \\ 4 & -6 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the main diagonal of $\matr{E}$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Find $m$, $n$ and $k$ in @def-main-diagonal.
